plain_text:
CITY OF SALEM, MASSACHUSETTS
Dominick Pangallo
Mayor
Scholarship & Education Committee Meeting – Draft Minutes
Monday, November 16, 2026, 6:30 P.M., meeting held remotely
Members Present: Yami Cruz, Gabby Bacha, Megan Cole, Josiah Guthrie, Lynne Mullen, Gabriel 
Yaeger
Staff Present: Lisa Peterson
Guest(s): None
1. Call to Order: 6:35 p.m.
2. Approval of August 10, 2026 Minutes: Josiah motioned to approve as submitted, Lynne 
seconded the motion, motion carried 5-0-0.
3. Financial Updates:
Taxpayer’s Education Fund Balance (as of September 14, 2026): $17,577.14
Taxpayer's Scholarship Fund Balance (as of September 14, 2026): $2,924.35
There were 0 new education fund application this month.
4. Education Fund Updates:
The education fund recipient from last month has received his award.
There were no new education fund applications this month.
5. Fundraising Discussion:
 Lisa has drafted a press release, and will publish it.  The press release is announcing the 
campaign “400 scholarship donations for the 400+”!  Community members will be invited 
to donate an amount corresponding to their high school graduation year (whether they 
graduated from a high school in Salem or elsewhere).  For example, someone who 
graduated in 1996 is encouraged to donate $19.96.  Someone who graduated in 2006 is 
encouraged to donate $20.06.  Anyone who is not able to donate the exact amount 
corresponding to their class year or who wants to donate a different amount should indicate
their class year in the memo line. At the end of the campaign, the class which has the 
highest number of participants will be invited to attend the annual scholarship recognition 
ceremony in the spring for a photo with the Mayor.
 Lynne gave a review of past fundraising ideas that the committee has tried.
 Josiah – Is it important to try to do a fundraising effort that is “October related”?  
Committee concludes that an October idea does not make sense for this year.
 Gabby set up a spreadsheet and a template for a QR code for businesses to raise money via
local businesses and restaurants.  This is a way to coordinate local efforts by local 
businesses to help support the scholarship fund.  The committee has the spreadsheet.
 Lisa: update on the “Donate Now” button – now when you click on it, you can go directly 
to “400 for the 400 campaign” – it is not yet where the committee wants it, but it is a work 
in progress
 Lisa will update the press release and send it out.
 Gabby will reach out to Fantasy Island in the interest of fundraising to further cultivate that
relationship as they often donate to the committee generously and without even being 
solicited.
 Someone from the committee may reach out to Doug Burke to reconnect with him now 
that he’s moved on to a new employer.
 Lisa should try to generate a QR code to give to Gabby related to donations.
 Reflections on the affinity group that Yami and Josiah recently attended.
6. Adjourned (5-0-0): 7:22 p.m.
